summary: Conjure a playable music video when the host has media-generation tools, with bounded local FFmpeg assembly as the last mile.
requires: For Conjure mode: a connected host capability able to generate moving video media; music/audio generation or a user-supplied finished song is also required
For local assembly: Python 3.10+, FFmpeg, FFprobe, and a writable workspace
A compatible media presentation surface if the result is expected to appear directly in chat
inputs: Conjure mode: the user's creative brief and either a supplied song or authority/capability to generate one
Assembly mode: one local JSON project manifest plus the referenced local audio and visual assets
An explicit output MP4 path when using the bundled renderer
outputs: Conjure mode: an actual playable music-video artifact from a capable host/provider
Assembly mode: a deterministic FFmpeg render plan and a verified H.264/AAC MP4
JSON media facts including duration, dimensions, byte length, and SHA-256 after local rendering

enforced: Local renderer: at most 300 shots and 20 minutes of declared timeline
Local renderer: at most 120 seconds per shot and 60 frames per second
Local renderer: even output dimensions, at most 3840 pixels per side, and at most 3840x2160 total pixels
Local renderer: each local input at most 2 GiB and all local inputs together at most 10 GiB
Local renderer: manifest inputs must resolve inside the manifest directory
Local renderer: existing output is not replaced unless --force is explicit
Local renderer: audio duration and trimmed video-source durations are probed before rendering
operator: Do not claim Conjure mode unless the current host actually exposes enough generation capability to produce moving video and required audio
Keep provider inference spend, remote retrieval, account writes, and publishing inside the user's authorized task scope
Review generated or retrieved media rights, likenesses, and platform requirements before distribution
Watch the complete export before making an artistic-quality or audience-playback claim

stop_when: The requested playable music video is produced and the available verification/review is complete
A required video-generation, audio, local asset, FFmpeg runtime, or presentation capability is absent
Another attempt would repeat a failed generation or render route without a concrete change
